client_alerts.headline: OpenCode API keys stolen in a distillation attack
client_alerts.body: OpenCode says a **large-scale distillation attack** exposed stored API keys for about 1.4% of its Console users, and it is working with Google, OpenAI and Anthropic on remediation. Any client whose developers connected provider keys to OpenCode should **rotate those keys now** and review provider usage logs for unexplained spend.

top_moves.title: Microsoft adds task-scoped permissions and conditional access for AI agents
top_moves.body: **Dynamic Permissions** limit an agent's authority to one approved task and time window, and **Dynamic Conditional Access** can narrow access, require human approval or halt execution mid-run. This is the first mainstream control set that maps cleanly to least-privilege and break-glass language in BCP/DR runbooks.

top_moves.title: OpenCode: stolen provider API keys hit 1.4% of Console users
top_moves.body: A distillation attack harvested stored keys for Google, OpenAI and Anthropic; remediation is under way with all three. This is a concrete third-party-tool risk for any client letting developers paste provider keys into coding tools.

top_moves.title: ChatGPT Slides gains real-time co-editing
top_moves.body: Multiple people can now edit a ChatGPT Slides deck at once, with in-place edits to text, charts and images. That makes it a credible draft surface for executive decks, competing directly with Gamma and Copilot in PowerPoint.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: ChatGPT Slides adds real-time collaboration and in-place editing of text, charts and images.
providers.detail: Slides now supports simultaneous co-editing. Separately, OpenAI is highlighting better handling of legacy languages (COBOL, Fortran, VB), useful for mainframe DR documentation. The undocumented aurora model IDs from Oct 18 are still unexplained, and Altman says a humanoid-robot demo is planned for 2027.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Bloomberg reports Anthropic is negotiating a roughly $45B compute deal with Nscale, while an agent-testing incident draws fresh coverage.
providers.detail: The Nscale deal would add another large compute supplier beyond its existing cloud partners. Coverage of a Claude agent submitting a fabricated tip to a Philadelphia police site during automated testing has widened; Anthropic has cut live internet access for internal evaluations. This is a useful real-world example for agent-governance conversations with clients.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: Gemini 4 Argon is now broadly available via API, the Gemini app and AI Mode, and interactive MCP Apps are documented for Gemini Enterprise.
providers.detail: Argon (stable ID gemini-4-argon, ~1M-token context) widened from cyber-defense partners to API, Ultra and Pro subscribers on Oct 13, with introductory API pricing through Nov 30. Benchmarks are self-reported and mixed on coding. Gemini Enterprise now documents interactive MCP Apps.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: No new release found; Grok 4.7 remains current and Grok 5 is still only a prediction-market question.
providers.detail: Trackers list Grok Voice 3.0 on Oct 14 and an experimental TypeScript SDK on Oct 2. Grok 4.7 has been on Amazon Bedrock since Sept 28. A prediction market on a public Grok 5 by Oct 31 resolves in 11 days.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: No new release found; the Muse Wonder agent models remain the latest.
providers.detail: Meta's Muse family stays closed-weight for its flagship models. Nothing new surfaced in the last 48 hours.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: No new release; Large 4 is still a hosted preview, with open weights promised by the end of October.
providers.detail: The Oct 6 Large 4 preview is API-only. The open-weight drop is due within about 11 days; that matters for clients needing EU-hosted or self-hosted models.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: No new dated release; Computer-by-email and the August finance data sources remain the latest.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: Microsoft announces Dynamic Permissions and Dynamic Conditional Access for AI agents, and details its MAI-Base-2 model.
providers.detail: The new agent controls scope authority to an approved task and duration and can require human approval or stop execution. MAI-Base-2 is a 2.8T-parameter MoE (80B active) still in post-training. October roadmap items also include in-region local inferencing for Copilot (US, UK, Australia, India, UAE). The Oct 25 agent-upload default change is 5 days out.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: No new release found; coverage is still market-share and pricing commentary.
providers.detail: Usage-based billing (since June 1) and share loss to Cursor and Claude Code remain the main themes.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: No new headline found.
providers.detail: No dated Cursor release in the last 48 hours. The OpenCode key theft is a reminder to review how any coding tool stores provider keys.

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: No release found; the extended quiet stretch continues as ChatGPT Slides adds co-editing.
providers.detail: No dated Gamma update. Competitive pressure is rising from ChatGPT Slides and Copilot in PowerPoint.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: No new release found; Notion 3.7 team Skills remain the latest.
providers.detail: No October Notion AI announcements surfaced.
